prompt: Data set P is $10$, $10$, $11$, $12$, $12$. Data set Q is $2$, $6$, $11$, $16$, $20$. Both have a mean of $11$. Which statement is true?

choices.label: P has the greater standard deviation
Q has the greater standard deviation
Standard deviation cannot be compared without more information

hint: Standard deviation measures how far the values sit from their mean.

hints.text: Standard deviation measures how far the values sit from their mean.
P's values are all within $1$ of the mean; Q's stretch $9$ away on each side.
Q is far more spread out, so Q has the greater standard deviation.

learningObjective: Compare standard deviations by inspecting spread.
explanation: Standard deviation measures typical distance from the mean — it is a spread measure, not a center measure.
Set P is tightly clustered: every value is within $1$ of $11$.
Set Q ranges from $2$ to $20$, with values as far as $9$ from the mean. So Q has the larger standard deviation.

alternativeExplanations.title: You never actually compute it
steps: The SAT never asks you to calculate a standard deviation by hand — only to compare two sets.
Look at how tightly the values cluster around their mean; tighter means smaller.
Equal means tell you nothing about spread, which is exactly why the question gives both sets the same mean.
